ideas.what: G_m^C-torsors P_{G,C} over boundary strata M_G built from tangent/normal lines at nodes and marked points, modelling punctured tubular neighbourhoods of strata (tangential base points at infinity)
ideas.modern_name: deleted tubular neighbourhood / normal torus bundle of a boundary stratum; tangential base points; real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama) boundary faces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura (1997); Harvey/Ivanov bordification; Kato–Nakayama log geometry
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (alludes to tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary and to 'groupoids at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower), without these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Functoriality of these torsors and their fundamental groupoids under graph contraction G → G/C, forming a ladder of cartesian squares
ideas.modern_name: functor from the category of stable graphs (with contractions) to groupoid extensions; modular-operad structure of mapping class groupoids

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a stratum neighbourhood as an extension of Π_1 M_G by Z^A (Dehn twists), with an additional Z^I for punctures
ideas.modern_name: stabilizer of a multicurve in the mapping class group = extension of a product of mapping class groups by the free abelian group of Dehn twists

ideas.what: Observation that the horizontal maps exist only in the homotopy category, not algebraically
ideas.modern_name: need for log geometry / formal neighbourhoods to algebraize the neighbourhood-to-generic-stratum maps (Kato–Nakayama spaces, log fundamental groups)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of torus torsors and Dehn-twist extensions along the stratification of M̄_{g,ν}. It is a nice early (c.1978–81) explicit version of what later became standard: Harvey bordification, multicurve stabilizers, the Ihara–Nakamura and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps formalisms. It is historically interesting as a precursor, but contains nothing absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ne sont définies que dans la catégorie topologique[?]' more likely reads 'dans la catégorie homotopique' (the maps are only defined up to homotopy).
'G→G' homom.[?] de généralisation de graphes NB.' should read '...de graphes MD' (Mumford–Deligne graphs). The symbol under G' is ≃ G/C.
In the formula P_{G,C} = ∏_{a∈C /M_G} P_{G,a}, the product is a fibre product over M_G.
In the bottom diagrams the unlabeled/struck symbol between SP_G and P_G is an arrow (SP_G → P_G ≃ P_{G,A}); the right-hand diagram has SRT_G ← ST_G (Z^A, 'cart.') and RT_G ← T_G (Z^A).
